result.summary: Do not ship: raw validation errors newly expose upstream response data in logs.

findings.title: Raw validation errors disclose sensitive response contents
findings.body: A 200 response containing {"password":"upstream-private-secret"} without version reaches SystemStatus.model_validate at line 218. Verified that its ValidationError includes the password in input_value; this change now logs it. The previous error-count message excluded response contents. collect_secrets (startup.py:74–99) collects only configured API/auth secrets, and both logging sinks perform literal replacement (logging.py:36–40,72–76), so unrelated upstream credentials survive into stderr and the web log buffer. A misrouted or malformed upstream response can therefore disclose sensitive data.
findings.recommendation: Restore count-only logging or emit allowlisted validation metadata without input values or context. Add a regression test asserting that sensitive fields in malformed responses never reach either logging sink.

next_steps: Remove raw validation exception logging and verify response-data redaction before merging.
